Q0295

“The clearer the knowing, the more earnest the practice; the more earnest…” — Zhu Xi (Zhuzi Yulei)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Zhuzi Yulei. Theme: knowledge.

Quotes / Zhu Xi / Q0295

English

The clearer the knowing, the more earnest the practice; the more earnest the practice, the clearer the knowing.

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Zhuzi Yulei and files it under Neo-Confucianism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Zhu Xi

Zhu Xi (1130–1200) was the Southern Song synthesizer of Neo-Confucianism whose commentaries on the Four Books became imperial orthodoxy for centuries. He organized cosmology of li (principle) and qi (vital stuff) and built academy pedagogy.

How to read this passage

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute. This passage enters that discussion through knowledge, practice.

Concepts in this quote

Knowledge
Knowledge is the philosophical study of what we can justifiably claim to know—and where certainty ends.
Practice
Practice is where thought becomes habit: philosophy as a way of living, training, and repeated action.
